description:
I'm a computer science student with experience in AI, software development, and geospatial data projects. Our goal is to build an engaging Mars exploration game using real NASA data, interactive missions, and scientific discovery.

We're looking for teammates interested in game development, Unity/Unreal, 3D modeling, UI/UX, planetary science, and creative storytelling. All skill levels are welcome. Let's explore Mars together!
summary: Solbound is a free English-language browser game for children aged 7–12. Players manage an outpost in Jezero Crater on Mars through a 30-sol mission. Each sol, they divide limited power between oxygen production, the greenhouse, radiation shielding and science, while considering when each decision will take effect. Players also control an astronaut in third person to clean solar panels, repair a loose connector, collect rock samples and bring them back for analysis. The game uses real NASA DONKI space-weather records and calculates Earth–Mars communication delay from JPL orbital elements. Real data, simplified models and game rules are clearly labelled. A skippable tutorial, six endings and a mission report help players understand the consequences of their choices. No account is required. All essential assets are bundled, and the game can also run offline through a local static server.
details:
Project Overview

Solbound is an English-language 3D Mars mission trainer for children aged 7–12. Players manage an outpost in Jezero Crater, keeping the crew alive through a 30-sol mission while earning at least 100 science points.

Built around the “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge, the game connects life support, power allocation, radiation shielding, food production and communication delay into one complete mission experience.

Core Gameplay: Every Power Block Requires a Choice

Each sol, the Console displays solar power output, night-heating needs and battery storage. Players divide limited power between four systems:

  • Oxygen production: meets the crew’s immediate oxygen needs.
  • Greenhouse: grows food that is harvested three sols later.
  • Shield construction: gradually upgrades the base and reduces subsequent radiation dose.
  • Science: builds scientific results and advances the mission goal.

These systems share one power budget. Increasing science investment leaves less power for other equipment, while building shielding early reduces future radiation risk. Leftover power charges the battery and provides reserves for later tasks.

Solar storms, dust storms, equipment faults and crop problems change the daily plan. Players examine environmental conditions and resource forecasts before adjusting their allocations.

Hands-on 3D Missions

Inside the habitat, players click physical objects to clean drinking water, obtain food, use medicine, contact Earth, analyse rock samples and end the day through the bed.

Outside, players control the astronaut in third person, move around the base and complete practical tasks:

  • Clean dust from solar panels.
  • Reconnect a loose power plug.
  • Scan the ground and save observations.
  • Collect rock samples and bring them back to the lab bench.

The results appear directly in the scene. Brown dust is wiped from the solar panels, the loose orange plug reconnects and turns green, and power output rises on the Console. Players can connect an equipment’s appearance, their own actions and the resulting resource changes.

How NASA Data Enters the Game

Solbound uses NASA data in events, resource decisions and scientific explanations.

  • NASA DONKI: real solar-flare and space-weather records form solar-storm events. At startup, the game attempts to retrieve flare data from the last 30 days and adds qualifying strong flares to the event pool.
  • Curiosity RAD: radiation measurements support explanations of the Martian surface environment and radiation shielding.
  • Perseverance MOXIE and MEDA: oxygen-production experiments and environmental information support explanations of oxygen production, Martian conditions and heating needs.
  • Opportunity, Spirit and InSight: mission records inform events involving dust accumulation, dust-devil cleaning, dust storms and marsquakes.
  • JPL orbital elements: Earth–Mars distance and communication delay are calculated for the current date, making “ask Earth for help” a choice that requires players to consider waiting time.

The in-game Data Sources page provides original links and separately labels live data, historical records and game models, allowing players to explore the scientific background behind their missions.

Educational Design and Creativity

Solbound lets players understand engineering trade-offs through action. Oxygen production meets immediate needs, the greenhouse requires advance planning, and shielding provides continuing benefits after construction. The value of an investment changes depending on when its results arrive.

The skippable first-sol tutorial follows the actual mission sequence: check power, repair equipment outside, return to clean water and drink, divide power, and end the day. Tutorial instructions correspond to equipment the player can currently see and actions they can perform.

Six endings and a mission report help players review their missions. Resource charts show changes in oxygen, food, radiation and science. Records of key decisions help players identify causes and develop a new strategy for their next attempt.

The project combines resource planning with hands-on work. Players decide whether to repair equipment and then walk to it to perform the repair. They address immediate survival needs while preparing for future harvests, storms and science goals.

Technical Implementation and Project Results

The game is built with HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript. Three.js renders the habitat, the Martian surface and mission animations. Toon shading, ink outlines and halftone effects create a consistent retro science-fiction style.

D3, TopoJSON and Natural Earth map data draw Earth in the opening sequence, while Web Audio synthesizes game sounds at runtime. Libraries, map data and fonts are bundled, supporting offline play through a local static server.

Solbound supports keyboard, mouse and touch controls, with an on-screen movement joystick for phones. The project includes a complete tutorial, a 30-sol mission, outdoor work, six endings and a mission report. A playable English version and the complete source code are publicly available.
